messages.text:
"Project Overview
A mobile optimized half casual flight simulator focusing on intuitive controls fun handling and visual satisfaction by omitting complex physics and procedures.
 * Controls and Input System
   Flight Control via mobile gyroscope tilt or virtual joystick for roll and pitch control.
   Auto Leveling feature that automatically corrects to horizontal when controls are released to prevent beginner crashes.
   Throttle Control using a right side vertical touch slider for smooth zero to one hundred percent power adjustment.
   Reverse and Brake buttons for quick stopping right after landing.
   Quick Action Buttons on the bottom right for boosters camera views and brakes.
 * Aircraft Lineup
   Airliner featuring heavy weight and stable handling specialized for smooth landing and passenger or cargo transport missions.
   Jet Fighter featuring agile mobility explosive acceleration and boosters specialized for aerial ring time attack and acrobatic flight.
 * Airfield Layout
   Runway as the central stage featuring centerlines number markings and night PAPI guidance lights.
   Airplane Hangar lobby area for selecting aircraft and starting missions.
   Control Tower and Terminal buildings providing large visual landmarks around the airport.
 * Environment and Visuals
   Time of Day settings offering Day with bright skies Evening with sunset lighting and Night with starlight and runway lights.
   Cloud Layer at mid altitude allowing players to fly through clouds during ascent for visual satisfaction.
   Earth Curvature effect displaying a naturally curved horizon when climbing to high altitudes with the jet fighter.
 * UI HUD and Game Loop
   Mobile Optimized HUD displaying speed altitude crosshair and horizon guidelines in the center.
   3D World Icons showing destinations runways and mission rings with remaining distance in meters or kilometers.
   Landing Evaluation system calculating touchdown impact and alignment to show Perfect Great or Bad feedback popups and rewards.


---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Built a complete, playable browser game in `index.html`. Choose the Skyliner or Afterburner, pick a time of day and landing or ring challenge, then fly with the on-screen joystick and throttle. Boost, camera, braking, keyboard controls, HUD, airport scenery, clouds, and landing feedback are included.

Assumptions: the game uses a lightweight, self-contained 2D canvas scene to keep it mobile-friendly and dependency-free. JavaScript syntax validation passed; I couldn’t verify the browser screenshot because Chromium isn’t installed in the environment.
